# Diagnostics

<!-- Generated by `cargo xtask diagnostics` from crates/slidock-ir/src/diagnostics/registry.rs: do not edit. -->

Every diagnostic slidock reports has a code (`MID5401`), a kebab-case name (`font-substituted`), a severity and a message. The CLI prints them on stderr, one per line:

```text
lossy   MID5401 font-substituted pp-256 pp-256.3: Calibri is not available; Carlito stands in
```

After the severity, code and name come the slide (or layout, or master) and the element it concerns, when there is one. `--emit report` lists them in `report.json`.

## Severities

| Severity | Meaning | Listed by the CLI |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `error` | The input could not be read, or a slide, layout or master (or the whole presentation) could not be converted and is left out. The CLI exits 1, or 2 for a refused input. | always |
| `decline` | An element is not shown at all: slidock does not support it. | by default |
| `lossy` | Something is shown, but differently from the original: approximated, simplified or partly left out. | by default |
| `warning` | The input is malformed or inconsistent; slidock worked around it. | by default |
| `info` | A note on how something was converted, which the deck shows faithfully or close to it. | with `-v` |

`-q` lists errors only. Whatever is not listed is counted in the summary line that follows the list.

## Codes

A code's letters name the part of slidock that reports it. In a message, `{name}` stands for a value the diagnostic fills in. *Feature* names the presentation feature whose loss the diagnostic reports, as `report.json` names it.
